DEFINITION · qeva:1:optimization@3

Optimization

A minimization problem specifies a feasible set and objective; its infimum is the optimal value and may be unattained.

editorialoptimization · analysis · algorithms
Run a related experimentTrace this conceptSearch connections

PLAIN

The idea

Optimization first specifies which choices are allowed and how they are scored; the best lower score may or may not be achieved by a choice.

EXACT

The compact statement

A minimization problem is specified by a feasible set X and objective f:X→Y into an ordered codomain. When it exists, inf f(X) is the optimal value. A global minimizer is x*∈X satisfying f(x*)≤f(x) for every x∈X; a finite infimum need not be attained.

Example

For f(x)=(x−3)² on R, the optimal value is 0 and the unique global minimizer is x=3.

Boundary / caveat

Mathematical optimality is relative to the chosen feasible set, objective, and order; it does not certify that those choices are appropriate.

Assumptions

  • A nonempty feasible set X and an objective f:X→Y are fixed. · Function @1
  • The codomain Y has enough order structure for the displayed comparisons and infimum. · Order @1
